headline: Microsoft is adding Word, Excel and PowerPoint to its redesigned Copilot app, so people can draft documents, build spreadsheets and make presentations there and keep the files in step with the Office apps.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: Microsoft's Copilot overhaul was reported on 9 Oct 2026, so the news is not new, and the Neowin piece dated 11 Oct could not be read to see whether it adds a rollout step.
importance_line: Office workers who write documents and spreadsheets are affected first, then IT teams who get new spending controls, then Microsoft, and the doubt is that the rollout is staged through the Frontier early-access programme and the report gives no date for when everyone gets Office in Copilot.
summary: IT Brief Australia reports that Microsoft's redesigned Copilot now brings Word, Excel and PowerPoint functions directly into Copilot, with files made there kept in sync with the Office apps so teams can keep working on the same documents. The report, from 9 Oct 2026, says this is part of a wider overhaul that adds a Home screen, a Code tool and a persistent agent called Autopilot, and that advanced agent work will be billed by use while everyday chat and Office use stays under the user's subscription.
notes: Neowin original blocked (HTTP 403); read IT Brief Australia's report of the same Microsoft announcement instead and credited it. TechEngage and Windows Report headlines (also blocked) confirm the Office-in-Copilot news. The exact Microsoft announcement date is not stated; the earliest report we could read is 9 Oct 2026.
